participants: Chris Klevan (sales manager, running the meeting)
Derek Harris (setter, first day on the team)
summary: Standard daily sales team meeting run by Chris Klevan: introductions for a new setter, a wins round, projection updates per rep, then roleplay training. Derek Harris is onboarded as a new setter (22, Virginia, prior setting and closing experience, introduced through a mutual friend of Chris). Kim Forbes-Sobers and Andrew Musial update their weekly set and cash projections; Andrew is told he needs $12,000 more — two more paid-in-full deals — with two selling days left, and Richard concedes he is behind ("I'm not doing what I should be doing yet"). The bulk of the call is a discovery roleplay in which Chris plays a 38-year-old, already-fit, already-coached prospect with minor tightness and Richard runs discovery on him, followed by detailed coaching from Chris and Andrew on how to handle an optimiser-type prospect who has no real pain. A second roleplay begins in which Andrew practises delivering the $6,000 price to a prospect who wants to think about it and shop around; the recording cuts off mid-exercise.
notable: Setter code DH is identifiable from this call: Derek Harris joined the team as a setter on 2026-07-07. The extraction spec currently records DH as unknown — anything suffixed DH from this date forward is Derek Harris. "I'm 22. I live in Virginia... I've worked on a couple of different offers, like between setting and closing, mostly setting, though. And I got linked up through this opportunity through kind of a mutual friend of me and Chris."

Kim Forbes-Sobers is confirmed as an active setter on the team and is the KFS suffix; she books directly into closers' calendars ("He's booked with Michael on Friday") and asked Richard and Andrew to confirm her sets while she is away for the rest of the week.

Chris Klevan's stated selling policy is explicitly against manufacturing need: "You can't make something look big enough that isn't there... You're not here to create something that isn't there. You're here to be a mirror to what is." He also endorses walking away — "it may just not make sense... let me send you a video that goes over everything" — rather than pushing a prospect with no goals.

Chris told Richard directly that he had attempted to manufacture a pain point in the roleplay: "A couple of moments, Richard, that you did on the call with me in that role play is you tried to manufacture something that wasn't there a couple of times... that was where we started to have a little bit of sticking points where I was like, no, like, it's fine, because it felt like you were pushing it to me."

A roughly $200/month product is treated as a sanctioned fallback in training, not an improvisation. Chris, roleplaying the prospect: "I expected it was going to be, like, $200 a month thing." Richard: "I can still run you through the two hundred a month and see if you're interested in that." Chris: "Yeah, yeah, yeah." This is the same tier Richard downsold to on the Nic call the previous day.
The $200/month figure is also identified as a widespread external anchor — it appears in this roleplay and in two live calls in this batch as the number prospects find before they call.
Targets are tracked as cash and paid-in-full units: Andrew was carrying $14K against a need for two more PIFs at $6,000 each; Kim moved sets between weeks four and five to hit 14 this week.
Chris Klevan disclosed a longstanding shoulder injury of his own and reported benching 185 for three reps; Kim pointed him to Trevor's shoulder mobility video.
Andrew Musial named payment processing and payment-objection handling as the single skill he most needs to work on; Richard named how he shows up on calls.

Chris coached a reframed consequence question for high-performing prospects: "it's not really a cost of inaction. It's a cost of staying good... if you were to stay exactly as you are, why is that not enough for you?" This is a script extension not present in playbook.json Phase 5.

Kim reported a prospect who came to kettlebells after a motorcycle accident that required both wrists to be completely reconstructed, and who is deferring 90 days for financial reasons; Chris responded "we got to get that guy in the program." No sale was made and no clinical question was raised.
